note: The one picture of 2017 Prairie this project reads whole (the Inland Architect's 1895 plate of Reid's house, next door at 2013, catches its north edge). A smooth stone front of two storeys over a high basement: on the north part, two pairs of tall square-headed lights a storey under a moulded cornice with a row of blocks, and over it a slated mansard with two gabled dormers (a pair of lights in the north one, one light in the other), each with pilasters and a carved lunette in its pediment, and a crenellated cresting along the mansard's curb; on the south part, a projection carried up into a steep gable with a finial and two attic lights; between them a porch of two columns with carved capitals carrying a deck whose parapet is pierced with rings, a ball finial on each corner; a high stoop with iron rails between stone newels; the basement's lights barred with iron grilles behind an iron railing along the front. It is undated and evidence of its own date; the 1911 Sanborn sheet draws the house in 1911 and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904, so its forms are carried to 1904 as inferred.
